mechanism_narrative: Rising housing starts (HOUST) indicate robust consumer demand for residential construction, which correlates with stronger corporate earnings growth and positive equity market sentiment, driving S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: HOUST growth exceeds 0.5% monthly but S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate increase above 4.0% per annum signals aggressive monetary tightening, which compresses equity valuation multiples through higher discount rates and reduced risk appetite, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS > 4.0% for 3 consecutive months yet S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous federal funds rate increases above 3.5% and unemployment rate declines below 4.0% indicate tight monetary policy combined with labor market strength, triggering inflation concerns and risk-off sentiment that depresses equity valuations over 60 trading days.
regime_hint: tight monetary policy with strong labor market
failure_condition: The joint condition (FEDFUNDS > 3.5% AND UNRATE < 4.0%) occurs but S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion regimes (UNRATE < 4.0% and GDP growth > 2.5% annualized), PAYEMS growth above 0.5% monthly signals labor market saturation, triggering inflationary pressure and central bank tightening that causes negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: Late-cycle expansion regime (UNRATE < 4.0% and GDP growth > 2.5% annualized) with PAYEMS growth > 0.5% monthly fails to produce negative 20-day returns in at least 60% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: Rising industrial production (INDPRO) indicates strengthening manufacturing output, which correlates with improved corporate profitability and positive market sentiment, driving S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO growth exceeds 0.3% monthly but S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A consumer spending decline exceeding 1.0% monthly (RSAFS) signals weakening demand for goods and services, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and triggers negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: RSAFS decline > 1.0% monthly but S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of such periods.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous consumer spending decline (RSAFS < -0.5% monthly) and inflation acceleration (CPIAUCSL > 0.5% monthly) signal stagflationary pressures, which trigger risk-off sentiment and negative equity returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint condition (RSAFS < -0.5% AND CPIAUCSL > 0.5% monthly) occurs but S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In supply-constrained regimes (INDPRO volatility > 1.5% and capacity utilization < 85%), rising INDPRO signals improving supply chain conditions, which boosts manufacturing output and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: Supply-constrained regime (INDPRO volatility > 1.5% and capacity utilization < 85%) with INDPRO growth > 0.3% monthly fails to produce positive 5-day returns in at least 60% of cases.
